# agentbus client API

> agentbus runs on your machine, between coding agents (Claude Code, codex) and their vendors.
> It records each step of their work as an event, in one local store.
> This API lets any program read those events, start agents, and write its own events.

This file is a short guide. The full reference is generated from the code when the service starts:
the OpenAPI 3.1 description at `GET /api/v0/openapi.json`, and an interactive page built from it at
`/docs`. Both are served by the service itself, without the token and without internet. There are no
client SDKs: call the endpoints directly, or generate a client from the description. The contract in
words is `docs/CLIENT_API.md` in the repository.

## Address and token

- The service listens on `http://127.0.0.1:8787` by default. `agentbus up -listen 0.0.0.0`
  makes it reachable from the network, such as from outside a container. With no port, 8787.
- Every request except `/api/v0/openapi.json` and `/docs` sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- The token is the file `token` in the data folder: `$AGENTBUS_HOME`, else
  `$XDG_DATA_HOME/agentbus`, else `~/.local/share/agentbus`.
- Never put the token in a URL. In a browser, read the stream with `fetch`, not `EventSource`.
- A browser page from any origin may call the API: CORS answers `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`
  and allows the `Authorization` header. No cookies are used; the token is the guard.
  `agentbus up -origin <url>` locks it to one origin.
- On loopback, the `Host` header must be `127.0.0.1:<port>`, `localhost:<port>` or `[::1]:<port>`,
  or the answer is 403. On another address any `Host` is accepted; the token is the guard.
- Every error is JSON: `{"error": "..."}`, with fixed wording.

```sh
TOKEN=$(cat "${AGENTBUS_HOME:-${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/agentbus}/token")
B=http://127.0.0.1:8787
```

## Inside a turn: `$AGENTBUS_URL` and `$AGENTBUS_TOKEN`

If you are an agent that agentbus started (`POST /api/v0/turns`), your environment has:

- `AGENTBUS_URL`: the service's address, such as `http://127.0.0.1:8787`.
- `AGENTBUS_TOKEN`: a token for your turn only. It reads **your own session** and nothing else,
  and stops working when your turn ends.

It works on: `GET /api/v0/turns` (your session's turns; `session` defaults to yours),
`GET /api/v0/turns/{id}/events`, `GET /api/v0/sessions/{your session}/events`,
`GET /api/v0/sessions/{your session}/search`, and `GET /api/v0/calls/{id}/context` and
`GET /api/v0/calls/{id}/pieces/{n}` for your session's calls. Anything else, every write
included, answers 403. Your session id is the `<session>` in your base URL
(`.../s/<session>/t/<turn>`, in `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` for claude), and every turn
`GET /api/v0/turns` lists carries it.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTBUS_TOKEN" "$AGENTBUS_URL/api/v0/turns"
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTBUS_TOKEN" "$AGENTBUS_URL/api/v0/sessions/abc/search?q=login"
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTBUS_TOKEN" "$AGENTBUS_URL/api/v0/calls/x-9f2c01ab-7/pieces/12"
```

## Starting up: snapshot, then stream

1. `GET /api/v0/sessions` returns every session and the `store` and `seq` it was computed at.
2. `GET /api/v0/events?store=<store>&after=<seq>` streams every event after that point, then new ones.

An event that lands between the two calls is in the stream, not in the snapshot. Nothing is lost or
counted twice. To resume after a disconnect, reconnect with the last `store` and `seq` you saw.

The cursor is the pair `store` and `seq`. If the `store` you send is not the current one, the answer
is 409 with the current `store` in the body: start over from step 1.

## Endpoints

### GET /api/v0/sessions

The sessions, newest activity first, with tokens, cost, open state and title. `agent` and `folder`
come from the session's latest turn that names them. `open` is true while a turn's agent for the
session is running. A session groups turns; `GET /api/v0/turns` lists the turns themselves.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $B/api/v0/sessions
# {"store":"st_9f2c…","seq":1041,"sessions":[{"id":"abc","agent":"claude","open":true,"turns":7,…}]}
```

### GET /api/v0/events

A live stream (`text/event-stream`). Each message is `id: <store>/<seq>`, `event: <kind>`,
`data: <one event as JSON>`, then a blank line. `: ping` comes every 15 seconds. `session=<id>`
limits it to one session. Without `store` and `after` it starts with new events only.

```sh
curl -sN -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$B/api/v0/events?store=st_9f2c…&after=1041"
```

### GET /api/v0/sessions/{id}/events

One session's stored events, oldest first, a page at a time. `limit` is 1 to 10000 (default 1000).
`next_after` is the `after` for the next page, or null.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$B/api/v0/sessions/abc/events?store=st_9f2c…&after=0&limit=100"
```

### POST /api/v0/turns

Start a turn. Without `session`: an agent (`claude` or `codex`) with a prompt in a folder, in a new
session. With `session`: the next turn of a session the snapshot marks `resumable`, in its own agent
and folder (send neither, or the session's own; a different one is refused with 400). Answers 202
as soon as it starts, with the session `id` and the new `turn` id. Every event of the turn carries
that id in `turn`, and its `turn.started` (with the prompt) is stored before the reply. `read_only`
is false unless true. True gives claude Read, Grep and Glob only, and codex `--sandbox read-only`.
False leaves claude its own tools and settings, and gives codex `--sandbox workspace-write` with
network on (`-c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true`): it can edit the folder and reach the
network, so it can call this API with its turn token. Read-only codex has no writes and no network. 404 for an unknown session, 409 when a turn is already running or the session
cannot be continued. At most 4 turns running at once (429). There is no `/api/v0/runs`. An agent
whose program is not on the service's PATH gets 400 and nothing is stored: `agent claude cannot
start: the program claude is not on the service's PATH. Install Claude Code and run claude once to
sign in, then try again. If it is installed, start agentbus from a shell where claude runs.`
`GET /api/v0/agents` shows which agents the service finds.

claude and codex both continue by own replay: the agent starts fresh, with no `--resume` or
`exec resume`, its `turn.started` names the earlier turn in `replay_from`, and the gateway puts
that turn's whole history in front of each of the turn's model requests. For claude that is
messages, tool calls, tool results and thinking blocks as sent and received. For codex it is input
items and the reply's output items, encrypted reasoning byte for byte, and the gateway also writes
the session's first thread id over the fresh one (body and headers) so the history is read from
cache. If it cannot, it stores `replay.failed` and the turn fails, rather than run without its
past. `replay_from` is always the newest turn. If that turn did not finish (its agent was stopped,
the service restarted mid-turn, or its last model call failed), the next turn still continues: the
history is what that turn did, with an error result for each tool call that got no result
(`tool_result`, or codex's `function_call_output` / `custom_tool_call_output`), then a note
starting `[Note from AgentBus, not written by the model]` (an assistant message for claude, a
developer message for codex) saying how it ended and to check the folder. A turn that never
reached the model adds the person's message and a note that it was not acted on. The next turn's
`turn.started` then carries `recovered_from` and `recovered_reason`. The 409 for a session that
cannot be continued gives the reason, naming the turn (such as one that may be missing events, or
whose last request was compacted). `agentbus up -replay=false` puts both on the vendor's resume (a
session already continued by replay is then refused with 409), and a session from before replies
were kept continues by the vendor's resume. A next turn's `turn.started` says which it used in
`continuity` (`replay` or `resume`).

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"agent":"codex","folder":"/Users/ana/Sites/x","prompt":"Review the last commit"}' $B/api/v0/turns
# {"id":"abc","turn":"t_5d0c…","base_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8787/s/abc/t/t_5d0c…"}
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"session":"abc","prompt":"Now fix the second one"}' $B/api/v0/turns
# {"id":"abc","turn":"t_91ee…","base_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8787/s/abc/t/t_91ee…"}
```

### GET /api/v0/turns

The turns, newest first, with `store` and `seq` like the sessions snapshot, so you can stream from
there. Each has `id`, `session`, `agent`, `folder`, `prompt`, `started`, `ended` (when done),
`state` (`running`, `finished`, `failed`), `outcome`, `exit_code`, `usage`, `cost_usd` and
`cost_complete`. A started turn's `state` comes from its agent's exit: 0 is `finished`, anything else
`failed`. `prompt` is the first 500 characters, with `prompt_truncated: true` when cut; the whole
prompt is the `text` of the turn's `turn.started` in `/turns/{id}/events`. `reply` is the first 500
characters of the reply to the turn's last model call, with `reply_truncated: true` when cut; it is
empty while that reply has not come. `model` is the model that last call asked for, and
`model_calls` counts the turn's `model.requested` events. `session=<id>` filters
to one session. `limit` is 1 to 1000 (default 100), and a page also stops at 4 MiB of rows; for
older turns send `before=<next_before>` until it is null.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$B/api/v0/turns?session=abc"
# {"store":"st_9f2c…","seq":1041,"turns":[{"id":"t_91ee…","session":"abc","state":"running",…}],"next_before":null}
```

### GET /api/v0/turns/{id}/events

One turn's stored events, oldest first, paged like a session's events. `events.dropped` names
sessions, not turns, so it is not among them. The same turn id can be in two sessions: send
`session=<id>` for one session's events only.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$B/api/v0/turns/t_91ee…/events?session=abc&store=st_9f2c…&after=0"
```

### GET /api/v0/sessions/{id}/search

Text search over one session's stored history, newest first. Searched: the messages and input
items of its model requests (tool calls and tool results among them), each once, in the first call
that carried it; each call's kept reply; and the text of `turn.started` (the prompt), of a
program's `x.*` events, and of a `model.responded` whose reply is not kept (or is kept without its request). Not searched: system
blocks, instructions, tool definitions (codex's `additional_tools` items included). Case is ignored; `q` is found as written (no regex).
`q` is 1 to 256 bytes. Each hit has `source` (`request`, `reply` or `event`), `turn`, `call`,
`piece`, `seq`, `kind`, `role`, `block` (such as `tool_result`), a `snippet` of up to 80
characters each side, and `read`: the path that returns the whole of it. `limit` is 1 to 200
(default 20); send `before=<next_before>` for older hits until it is null. A page can hold fewer
than `limit` hits and still have a next page.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$B/api/v0/sessions/abc/search?q=login&limit=5"
# {"store":"st_9f2c…","hits":[{"source":"request","turn":"t_5d0c…","call":"x-9f2c01ab-7","piece":12,"seq":1042,
#   "kind":"message","role":"user","block":"tool_result","snippet":"…func Login(…","read":"/api/v0/calls/x-9f2c01ab-7/pieces/12"}],"next_before":null}
```

### GET /api/v0/calls/{id}/context

Everything one model call's request carried, piece by piece, with sizes. `{id}` is the `exchange`
of the call's events. `full=false` leaves out each piece's `json`.

### GET /api/v0/calls/{id}/pieces/{n}

One piece of a call: `n` is its index in the context's `pieces`, from 0, or `reply` for the kept
reply. The body is the piece's bytes exactly as stored (`application/json`); `X-Piece-Kind`,
`X-Piece-Hash`, `X-Piece-Count` and `X-Piece-Label` describe it. 404 when there is no such piece.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$B/api/v0/calls/x-9f2c01ab-7/pieces/reply"
```

### POST /api/v0/events

A program writes its own event. `kind` is `x.<program>.<name>`; `session` is a known session or
`default`. Answers 201 with `seq` and `id`.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"kind":"x.review.finding","session":"abc","text":"Line 12 reads past the end.","data":{"line":12}}' \
  $B/api/v0/events
```

### GET /api/v0/agents

Which agents this service can start: found on PATH, version, signed in.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $B/api/v0/agents
```

### GET /api/v0/openapi.json

The OpenAPI 3.1 description, generated from the code at startup, with JSON Schemas for every body
and every event kind. No token.

```sh
curl -s $B/api/v0/openapi.json
```

## Events

Every event has `seq`, `id`, `kind`, `time`, `exchange` and `vendor`, and usually `session`. Other
fields depend on the kind. Ignore kinds and fields you do not know: v0 may add both.

| kind | what happened | main fields |
|---|---|---|
| `turn.started` | a person's message started a turn | `turn`, `text`, `agent`, `folder` (empty when the turn was not started through `POST /api/v0/turns`), `replay_from` (the earlier turn a replayed turn continues), `continuity` (`replay` or `resume`, on a next turn), `recovered_from` and `recovered_reason` (the previous turn did not finish and how it ended; this turn continues after it) |
| `model.requested` | the harness sent a request to the model | `model`, `tools_offered`, `replayed` (history messages the gateway put in front) |
| `model.responded` | the model replied | `status`, `text`, `stop_reason`, `usage`, `cost_usd`, `cost_complete`, `error` |
| `tool.requested` | the model asked for a tool | `tool_id`, `tool_name`, `tool_input` |
| `tool.completed` | a tool's result reached the model | `tool_id`, `tool_output`, `tool_error` |
| `turn.completed` | the turn ended | `outcome` (`finished`, `partial`, `refused`, `unknown`), `stop_reason` |
| `session.opened` | a turn's agent started | `hold`, `agent`, `folder`, `turn` |
| `session.closed` | a turn's agent exited | `hold`, `exit_code`, `resume_id`, `turn`, `unsettled` (its calls may not all be stored) |
| `session.registered` | older stores only; nothing writes it now | `agent`, `folder` |
| `events.dropped` | events were lost; those sessions' costs are incomplete | `dropped`, `sessions`, `all_sessions` |
| `schema.unexpected` | the vendor sent a shape the adapter does not know | `unexpected` (`where`, `value` or `field`) |
| `replay.failed` | a replayed turn's request could not be given the earlier turn's history; the gateway refused it and the turn fails | `error` |
| `x.<program>.<name>` | a program's own event | `text`, `data`, `turn`; `vendor` is `program` |

- `usage` is absent when the vendor sent none. Absent is not zero.
- Match a `tool.completed` to its `tool.requested` by `tool_id`, never by `turn`.
- A turn started through `POST /api/v0/turns` has the id the reply named on every event, however
  many model calls its agent makes. Traffic pointed at the gateway by hand gets a turn id hashed
  from the conversation.
- A turn's agent may end several model calls with `turn.completed`; its `state` in `GET /turns`
  comes from the agent's exit.
- `probe`: true on every event of a harness's own check, such as Claude Code's startup
  quota check. It has no turn. A cockpit may hide it.
